subtitulo: Two ways to say _hardly_. One works alone; the other never goes out without its no.
regla: Apenas goes alone before the verb, or after it with no in front. Casi always takes no, in that order: casi no.

bloques.texto: To say _hardly_, _barely_ or _hardly ever_, Spanish uses **apenas** or **casi no**. They mean the same thing, but they don't sit in the sentence the same way.
Object pronouns go between **apenas** or **casi no** and the verb: **==apenas la== conozco**, **==casi no te== oigo**.
Tip: **apenas** is independent and goes out alone. **Casi** never goes out without its **no**.

secciones.titulo: Apenas: alone, or at the end

bloques.texto: The usual place is **right before the verb**, and the sentence stays affirmative, with no **no**.

lista.es: Después de rolar, ==apenas puedo== levantar los brazos.
lista.en: After rolling, I can barely lift my arms.

lista.es: A la vecina nueva ==apenas la conozco==.
lista.en: I hardly know the new neighbor.
Do you see Beto a lot? No, I hardly see him.

lista.es: Con la neblina ==apenas se ve== el pico.
lista.en: With the fog you can barely see the peak.

bloques.texto: You can also build it like [[5136|**nunca**]]: **no** before the verb and **apenas** after it. This is Spanish double negation, and it's correct.

lista.en: Beto hardly ever cleans his room.

bloques.texto: In summary, you have two options: **apenas** + an affirmative sentence, or **no** + verb + **apenas**.

secciones.titulo: Casi no: always together, always in that order

bloques.texto: **Casi** does the same job, but it **always needs the verb in the negative**: **casi no** + verb. Without the **no**, the sentence no longer means _hardly_.

lista.es: Entre semana ==casi no tengo== tiempo para surfear.
lista.en: I hardly have time to surf during the week.

lista.es: ==Casi no visito== a mis papás porque viven en Ensenada.
lista.en: I hardly ever visit my parents because they live in Ensenada.

lista.es: En temporada baja Beto y yo ==casi no nos vemos==.
lista.en: In the off-season Beto and I hardly see each other.

lista.es: ==Casi no te oigo==, se está cortando la llamada.
lista.en: I can barely hear you, the call is breaking up.

lista.es: Nosotros ==casi nunca== nos peleamos; nos llevamos increíble.
lista.en: We hardly ever fight; we get along great.

bloques.texto: With **casi**, the **no** goes **after** it, right next to it, and both go **before the verb**. You can't swap them, split them, or leave the **no** out.

filas.t: No casi tengo tiempo para leer.
Casi no tengo tiempo para leer.
No tengo tiempo casi para leer.
Casi no tengo tiempo para leer.

lista.nota: **Casi** can't move to the end the way **apenas** can.

filas.t: Casi tengo el dinero para la tabla.

lista.nota: Without **no**, **casi** isn't _hardly_ anymore. It's _almost_: you almost have it. See [[8630|**por poco** and **casi**]].

lista.texto: The shortest. **Apenas** alone, before the verb.
The everyday one in Mexico. Always **casi no**.
Double negation, like [[5136|**nunca**]]. You hear it less, but the quiz asks for it.

secciones.titulo: Other meanings of apenas and casi

lista.forma: Por poco me caigo de la tabla.
lista.texto: [[8630|**Por poco** / **casi**]] + present: _nearly_, something that almost happened and didn't.
Another **apenas**: _as soon as_. See [[8294|**en cuanto**, **apenas**, **tan pronto como**]].
The same double negation: [[5136|**nunca** in negative sentences]].
Other quantity words with a verb: [[6135|**demasiado**, **bastante**, **poco**, **mucho**]].

bloques.texto: Say it out loud, then open the answer.

lista.p: Which one? **No casi tengo tiempo** or **Casi no tengo tiempo**.

lista.nota: **Apenas** before the verb takes no **no**. **No te oigo apenas** also works.

lista.p: In Spanish: _I hardly know him._ Say it both ways with **apenas**.
lista.r: Apenas lo conozco. / No lo conozco apenas.
lista.nota: Alone before the verb, or at the end with **no** in front.

lista.p: **Yo casi no salgo**: very little, or almost always?
